documents.unit: Office of Information Technology (MyCGU AI guidance)
documents.title: Guidance for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the application of AI to CGU
documents.summary: High-level university guidance that welcomes AI use, lists six guiding principles, announces a ChatGPT EDU license, and allows free AI tools if data privacy policies are followed. It sets no course-level rules on student work and links to other policies.
documents.stance_why: The page says "ignoring AI isn’t just unrealistic" and the community is "welcome to use the free versions of AI tools" "as long as" privacy policies are followed, so AI is allowed with a condition (permit). It does not delegate to instructors or set tiers.

units.why: The page says "ignoring AI isn’t just unrealistic—it could mean missing out", which treats AI engagement as expected; default-permissive, so P02, and informs because it is a rationale, not a rule.
units.anchor: ignoring AI isn’t just unrealistic

units.why: The page "aims to provide high-level info, policy, and considerations" for the whole community, which frames the purpose and scope of CGU's guidance; P56 (framework/preamble), not P04 since no one is delegated.
units.anchor: high-level info, policy, and considerations for using AI effectively

units.why: The page recognizes "the landscape is constantly evolving" and says "thoughtful engagement is the best path forward"; it names no review cycle, so P56 fits better than P54.
units.anchor: thoughtful engagement is the best path forward

units.why: The university says it will "explore and apply AI in ways that enhance teaching, learning, research, and institutional innovation", an institution-level statement of purpose that welcomes AI; P56 as preamble.
units.anchor: explore and apply AI in ways that enhance teaching, learning, research, and institutional innovation
units.frag_start: Claremont Graduate University leverages the collective

units.why: The strategy is "principled and adaptive—balancing innovation with ethical responsibility"; a framework-level principle, so P56 rather than P53 since it names no specific harm.
units.anchor: balancing innovation with ethical responsibility
units.frag_start: CGU’s AI strategy is principled and adaptive

units.why: Guiding principle 1 reads "People, not technology, must be at the center of our work", a principle in the institution-wide framework (P56) with a must modality.
units.anchor: People, not technology, must be at the center of our work

units.why: Principle 2 says the technology "must be easily accessible to people from diverse backgrounds"; access is the content, so P51 fits better than generic P56.
units.anchor: easily accessible to people from diverse backgrounds
units.frag_start: This technology must be easily accessible

units.why: Principle 3 states "Digital and information literacy is an essential part of a core education"; P44 is close but it is not framed as an employer expectation, so P56 as a framework principle.
units.anchor: Digital and information literacy is an essential part of a core education

units.why: Principle 4 says "AI tools should enhance teaching and learning"; a framework principle with should modality.
units.anchor: AI tools should enhance teaching and learning

units.why: Principle 5 holds that "Learning about technologies is an experiential, lifelong process"; a framework principle, not a rule on use.
units.anchor: Learning about technologies is an experiential, lifelong process

units.why: Principle 6 says "AI research and development must be done responsibly", which governs AI in research, so P62 fits better than P56.
units.anchor: AI research and development must be done responsibly

units.why: The university "has acquired a ChatGPT EDU license" giving the community access, a sanctioned, provided AI tool (P17).
units.anchor: Claremont Graduate University has acquired a ChatGPT EDU license

units.why: The license offers "enhanced security and privacy protections" so interactions "remain confidential"; this points to a vetted tool for privacy, P50.
units.anchor: enhanced security and privacy protections, ensuring that interactions with AI remain confidential

units.why: The community "is welcome to use the free versions" of ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot "as long as" they comply with data privacy policies; permission with a privacy condition, P50 chosen over P02 because the condition is the operative content.
units.anchor: welcome to use the free versions of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini

units.why: The table is introduced as policies that "communicate the requirements and expectations of the CGU community", pointing to the Appropriate Use, FERPA and other policies; an institution-level framework pointer, P56.
units.anchor: communicate the requirements and expectations of the CGU community
units.frag_start: CGU guidelines are formal statements of intent

documents.title: AI - Center for Academic & Faculty Excellence
documents.summary: Teaching-center resource page that supports faculty in using AI and points to a SharePoint, webinars and a curated reading list. It states no rules for student work.
documents.stance_why: CAFE "supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence" and curates resources, which welcomes AI use without conditions beyond academic integrity and ethics, so encourage.

units.why: CAFE "supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence while maintaining academic integrity, ethical responsibility, and intellectual ownership"; faculty support under stated values, P63, encouraging.
units.anchor: supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence

units.why: The page invites faculty to "Connect with other faculty to discuss AI, academics, and scholarship", a faculty community for learning about AI (P63).
units.anchor: Connect with other faculty to discuss AI, academics, and scholarship
units.frag_start: Connect with other faculty to discuss

units.why: OIT's SharePoint is "designed for the CGU community to explore OpenAI capabilities", a provided resource tied to the sanctioned AI tool, P17.
units.anchor: designed for the CGU community to explore OpenAI capabilities

units.why: CAFE offers "curated AI-related webinars that empower your teaching", a faculty learning resource (P63).
units.anchor: curated AI-related webinars that empower your teaching and deepen your learning

units.why: The curated list covers "teaching writing in light of AI technology" including sample policy statements and detection; faculty support to learn about AI before setting policy, P63.
units.anchor: extensive resources for teaching writing in light of AI technology
units.frag_start: This community driven resource list has

notes: Coder B. The CAFE page mostly lists third-party readings; external quotes (e.g. the Mollick passage on designing assessment that incorporates AI-generated text) were not coded as CGU policy. The academic integrity standards page was not collected, so no misconduct rules are coded.
